feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: it communicates scope, progression, and platform leadership clearly. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add impact.  
- Broad yet coherent skill profile: strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are presented as a consistent leadership narrative.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across sections: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve focus.  
- Add more outcome-based achievements: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; include measurable impact where possible (growth, efficiency, engagement, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; date formats vary (“Sept.”/“Mar.”/“Oct.”), “organization-wide” vs. other compounds should stay consistent, and “English (Native)” / “French (A2/Learning)” would read more cleanly as “Native” / “A2 (learning).” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and repeats several competency areas already covered elsewhere. It would be stronger with one concrete scale marker and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct leadership language: “leading” or “delivering.”
- Add one concrete proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views.”
- Trim the long capability list to 3–4 priority themes most relevant to target roles.
- Consider this rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for public-sector and membership organizations. Leads website transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure and editorial operations, with recent experience delivering a 10,000+ page Drupal migration, scaling publisher workflows and shaping AI-enabled search and content experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance models/content operations/editorial systems” overlaps heavily with Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- “Multimedia production” is already well covered in Work Experience and skills sections.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and phrased with parallel structure.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper noun phrases and keep all items in a consistent format.
- Emphasize highest-value strengths most aligned with recent roles: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, and cross-channel operations.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Replace “Multi-channel” with “Cross-channel” for a more current, polished feel; change “platform integration” to plural for consistency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” and “multimedia production” are already prominent in the header and Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills; keep only if this audience values sector specialization.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope where possible will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements
- Add dates or “Selected Recent Projects” framing to reinforce recency and distinguish this from core experience.
- Use parallel, punchier phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and trim stacked nouns (e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and AI chat”).
- Clarify scale or result where available: audience, campaign purpose, conference/event context, or ongoing use.
- Standardize style: spell out “10 x 20-foot,” keep capitalization consistent, and consider “AI-powered” instead of “AI-enabled” for smoother wording.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially repeat achievements already covered in the current freelance and NACo roles.
- If kept, position this as “Selected Projects” with more specific outcomes/examples rather than restating responsibilities.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, content operations, and AI-enabled search.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership language: “Built,” “Led,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Established.”
- Consolidate into 3–4 bullets, e.g.:
- Led Drupal-based campaign and storytelling builds, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Built communications workflows, analytics, and governance practices to improve cross-channel coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Delivered front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties, improving publishing reliability and usability.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user-facing discovery.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, publishing time reduced, engagement lift, search success, or stakeholder adoption.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry focused on leadership/ownership, not project detail.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement also echo prior NACo roles; emphasize what is new in this consulting engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. Tighten the opening, make outcomes more explicit, and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to emphasize transformation + scale: “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add outcome language where possible: for analytics/governance, specify reporting speed, decision-making improvements, publishing consistency, reduced bottlenecks, or stronger cross-team adoption.
- Condense channel bullet: focus on ownership and audience scale, not routine management. Example: “Oversaw email and social programs reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this role focused on enterprise leadership and modernization.
- Video production/studio language may duplicate older NACo bullets; emphasize building institutional capability, not producing content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more specific to operational leadership and channel growth during 2018–2022, with sharper outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and progression: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy publishing during a period of organizational growth.”
- Tighten bullets and front-load impact: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet outcome-focused: “Launched and grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across NACo’s digital platforms.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems point: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, increasing consistency across communications, advocacy and program content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial planning” echo the Director role’s “governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.”
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent roles. It should be tighter and more distinctive, emphasizing leadership scope rather than repeating generic digital/content phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & governance
- Editorial operations for multi-publisher teams
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy and member messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Change “Editorial systems and governance” to “Editorial operations for multi-publisher teams” to better reflect the 50+ internal publishers context.
- Change “Audience-focused content planning” to “Audience-centered content strategy” for a more senior, topline tone.
- If space allows, add scale in parentheses to one line, e.g. “Editorial operations for multi-publisher teams (50+ publishers).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “governance” already appear in the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications” in Core Competencies.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-list-heavy and overlaps heavily with the Technical + IT section. Make it more selective and outcome-oriented, emphasizing recent strengths in Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, automation, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from software inventory to capability-led phrasing: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older platforms here unless central to target roles; keep Drupal first, and move WordPress/SharePoint/Power Pages to Technical + IT only.
- Remove “jQuery” from this topline section unless specifically required by the job; it dates the profile and is already covered by broader front-end capability.
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work, e.g., “enterprise Drupal modernization” or “AI-enabled search and discovery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it in only one topline area if space is tight.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to a capability-led line, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity for KPI design, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis and digital optimization”
- Put the highest-value business outcomes first: “KPI design” and “executive/leadership reporting” should lead, with tools supporting them.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented term such as “analytics infrastructure” or “optimization insights” to connect with recent NACo work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool list elsewhere; use this section for strategic analytics strengths, and keep the full stack in Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems

- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and recent leadership-level multimedia strengths rather than generic production terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery

- Broadcast-quality video production and editing
- Livestream and hybrid event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” duplicates “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies
- “Video production and editing” overlaps with “Multimedia & Creative Tools” and multiple NACo experience bullets; avoid repeating tool-level detail here

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should either add specificity or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise/public-sector), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: “Drupal site builds/migrations • WordPress • SharePoint intranets • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful project; it feels lighter than the rest.
- If you want more impact, combine with adjacent technical item: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages • CMS modernization • front-end implementation.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly duplicated by Topline Skills > “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same tools plus stronger context.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles; avoid repeating the same platform names in multiple sections without added detail.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Front-End & Technical Implementation”
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: “HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, add scope/level instead of just tools: “Front-end development for Drupal/WordPress, lightweight scripting, deployment automation, and third-party integrations”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; they date the section without adding value

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep one version shorter or consolidate
- “GitHub Actions” and “Cloudflare Workers” are useful differentiators—prioritize keeping those over more generic items if space is tight

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation”/“Airtable systems” already called out elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize automation platforms over general collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools”
- Reorder by relevance/strength: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”
- Drop lower-value or dated items unless central to recent work: Basecamp, Trello
- If accurate, add light specialization instead of more tools, e.g. “Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana (project workflows)”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing verbatim.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; including both is fine, but they add less value than automation/integration platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and, if possible, signal enterprise use rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights & Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: Enterprise email automation • newsletter distribution • member engagement workflows
- Keep platform names only if these are tools you directly used/administered; otherwise remove the weakest/oldest platform

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “audience engagement,” or campaign management language here; that’s already covered in Work Experience.
- If Higher Logic was the primary NACo platform, consider dropping Mailchimp unless it reflects recent freelance or hands-on use.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant stack for the target roles, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Tighten it to emphasize tools over broad concepts and align with the stronger, recent analytics achievements in NACo and consulting roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • Google Optimize/other A/B testing tools
- Replace broad terms like “SEO,” “A/B testing,” and “Dashboarding” with specific platforms or methods; if no named tools, use “SEO analysis” and “experiment design.”
- Order by strongest/recentest capability: analytics stack first, then behavior insights, then optimization.
- If space allows, add one qualifier in the section title or elsewhere, e.g., “Analytics, Reporting & Optimization,” to better match the actual content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping detail in one place only.
- “Dashboarding” is already implied by Looker Studio and Power BI, so it adds little value.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to early-team building, web refresh support, and hands-on production.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and contribution: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or workflow improvements.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce abstractions: replace “high-impact digital content” with named deliverables like “livestreams, weekly advocacy videos, and multimedia content.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard/manage,” depending on authority.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early production support, while the later role shows scaling.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia” is similar to later operations bullets; keep this version narrower and more tactical.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific line such as “Produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or types of stakeholders served.
- Keep this entry concise since later roles show greater digital leadership; 1–2 lines is enough.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production” repeats strongly with later NACo roles; keep the focus here on podcast launch and innovation/research coordination.
- Avoid broad “digital communications” language already covered in 2015–2024 entries.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia & Creative Software
- Rewrite as: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to keep capabilities, split them into a separate item: Livestream production • Studio workflows • Podcast production
- Only retain tools you actively used in recent roles; if applicable, add one stronger platform/tool instead of generic workflow language
